metadata.name: cut
metadata.description: Extract columns or fields from files

installation.note: cut is a built-in command available on all Linux systems by default

overview.summary: cut extracts columns or fields from files. It can extract by character position or by delimited fields (like CSV). Simpler than awk for basic column extraction, but less powerful. Essential for processing structured data and extracting specific columns.

syntax.description: Extract columns from FILE (or stdin). Use -d for delimiter, -f for fields, or -c for characters.

options.use_case: Process CSV or other delimited files

examples.title: Extract column from CSV
examples.description: Get second column from CSV file

output_explanation.notes: Extracts second column from CSV. -d specifies delimiter, -f specifies field number. Essential for CSV processing.

examples.use_case: Extract columns from CSV and delimited files

examples.title: Extract first column

breakdown.useful: Extract first column from space/tab-separated files

output_explanation.notes: Extracts first field. Default delimiter is tab. Useful for space/tab-separated files.

examples.use_case: Extract first column from space/tab-separated files

examples.title: Extract by character position
examples.description: Get first 10 characters of each line

breakdown.position: Extracts by character position, not fields

output_explanation.notes: Extracts by character position. Useful for fixed-width files or extracting prefixes.

misconceptions.title: cut works like awk
misconceptions.misconception: cut and awk work the same way
misconceptions.reality: cut is simpler - just extracts columns. awk is more powerful - can process, calculate, filter. Use cut for simple extraction, awk for complex processing.
misconceptions.tip: cut = simple column extraction. awk = powerful processing. Use cut for simple cases, awk for complex.

common_pitfalls.description: cut fails on CSV without -d flag
common_pitfalls.solution: Always use cut -d',' for CSV files. Default delimiter is tab, not comma.

related_commands.relationship: Column extraction; cut for simple, awk for complex
related_commands.description: Text processing (more powerful than cut for complex operations)

best_practices: Use cut -c for character position extraction
Use cut for simple column extraction, awk for complex processing
performance_tips: Simpler and faster than awk for basic extraction

additional_notes.delimiter: Default delimiter is tab. Use -d to specify (comma, colon, pipe, etc.)
additional_notes.vs_awk: cut = simple column extraction. awk = powerful processing. Use cut for simple cases.
additional_notes.common_patterns: Very common: cut -d',' -f2 file.csv (CSV column), cut -f1 file (first field), ps aux | cut -d' ' -f1 (extract from command output)
